subject.title: Clarify or preserve skill source provenance from CLI publish

question: Should CLI-supplied repository metadata remain non-visible/non-trusted, become explicitly labeled untrusted attribution, or gain a server-verified provenance path?
rationale: Each option establishes a different public trust claim and verification obligation; the existing boundary deliberately prevents client declarations from being promoted implicitly.

options.title: Document the current trust boundary
options.body: Retain server-resolved provenance as the only trusted signal and make CLI help and publishing documentation state that source flags do not create verified or necessarily visible provenance.

options.title: Expose untrusted attribution separately
options.body: Store and render publisher-declared source information under a clearly unverified field that never affects verify or trusted-signal UI.

options.title: Add verified CLI provenance
options.body: Define a server-side ownership and content-verification protocol before allowing CLI source declarations to populate trusted provenance.

recommendation.title: Document the current trust boundary
recommendation.body: Retain server-resolved provenance as the only trusted signal and make CLI help and publishing documentation state that source flags do not create verified or necessarily visible provenance.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged GitHub-backed source-sync work is the strongest available ownership signal for the existing server-resolved provenance model.
